# E0337: type of the wrong kind

A constructor trait's parameter stands for a generic type, so it is written with its type arguments, as `F<i64>`.

- Rule: [`traits.constructor-traits`](../../reference/11-traits.md#traits.constructor-traits)
- Reported at: the type, or the bound that mixes kinds.
- Tier: `advanced`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0337:5
trait Mappable {
  fn transform<A, B>(self: Self<A>, f: fn(A) -> B) -> Self<B>
}

fn size<F: Mappable>(xs: F) -> i64 { 0 }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
trait Mappable {
  fn transform<A, B>(self: Self<A>, f: fn(A) -> B) -> Self<B>
}

fn size<F: Mappable>(xs: F<i64>) -> i64 { 0 }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0337_type_of_the_wrong_kind.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0337_type_of_the_wrong_kind.lt):

```text
── TYPE OF THE WRONG KIND ──────── E0337_type_of_the_wrong_kind.lt:5:26  [E0337]

`F` is a constructor of 1 type argument, so it is written with them, as `F<…>`:

  5 │ fn size<F: Mappable>(xs: F) -> i64 { 0 }
    │                          ^

A constructor trait's parameter stands for a generic type, so it is written with
its type arguments, as `F<i64>`.
```
